● The log shows you created a Cloudflare Worker project, not a Pages project,
  and that is why the deploy failed.

  - No build ran. It says "No dependencies detected" and went straight to npx 
    wrangler deploy, because the build command was empty. The Worker flow also
    doesn't use the build command from SETUP.md.
  - No output folder. wrangler deploy had no apps/web/dist to upload, and the
    repo has no wrangler config, hence "Could not detect a directory containing
    static files".
  - SETUP.md is out of date. Cloudflare's dashboard now steers new projects to
    Workers, and SETUP.md section C doesn't warn you about that. I'll add a note
    once this is sorted.

  Option 1: recreate as a Pages project (recommended)

  This matches the spec and DECISIONS.md, and needs no code change.

  1. In Cloudflare, open Workers & Pages, then Create application. Look for a
     small link such as "Looking to deploy Pages? Get started" and click it.
     Cloudflare moves things around, so the exact label may differ.
  2. Choose Import an existing Git repository, then pick Chalo.
  3. Enter these settings:
     - Production branch: main
     - Framework preset: None
     - Build command: corepack enable && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm 
       --filter @chalo/web build
     - Build output directory: apps/web/dist
     - Environment variables: NODE_VERSION=24, VITE_STORAGE_CAP_MB=900,
       VITE_SUPABASE_URL=unset, VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=unset, and VITE_APP_URL
       set to the URL it gives you.
  4. Delete the failed Worker project so it doesn't confuse things later.

  Option 2: keep the Worker project

  I'd add a small wrangler.jsonc to the repo that serves apps/web/dist with SPA
  fallback. You'd also set the build command above in the project's build
  settings. This is a bigger change: the spec says Pages, so I'd have to update
  SPEC.md and DECISIONS.md, and PR preview URLs would work differently.

  What I need back

  After the first deploy succeeds:
  - the final public URL;
  - whether the PR #1 preview comment or check now shows up.

  I'll then verify the headers, the SPA fallback and the offline page myself.

  yet. The later ones (VITE_APP_URL, the Supabase pair, VITE_STORAGE_CAP_MB) are
  listed in SETUP.md. Keep Web Analytics and Speed Insights off (PRV-006).

  Files outside the root directory

  The web app imports @chalo/core, which is a symlink to packages/core, and
  extends tsconfig.base.json at the repo root. Vercel's docs say a project can't
  read files outside its Root Directory. Leaving Root Directory at ./ solves
  it. If you ever set it to apps/web, you'd also have to enable Include files 
  outside of the Root Directory in the Build Step and move vercel.json. SETUP.md
  explains this.

  Why Corepack

  Vercel's automatic pnpm detection only covers pnpm 6 to 10, and this repo pins
  pnpm@12.11.2. A plain pnpm install override would use the oldest pnpm, so I
  set the Corepack variable above. If Corepack fails on Vercel, SETUP.md has a
  fallback (npx pnpm@12.11.2 …). I haven't tested that fallback either.

● The labels in your dashboard may differ from what I said, so I used Vercel's
  current docs. This is the page and what it should contain.

  Where to go

  Open this link while signed in to Vercel:
  https://vercel.com/project-f671/chalo/settings/deployment-protection

  Or go to the chalo project, then Settings in the left sidebar, then Deployment
  Protection.

  What you should see

  - A Vercel Authentication section with an on/off toggle.
  - A choice of which deployments it covers. The labels are Standard Protection,
    All Deployments, and possibly older ones marked (Legacy).

  How Vercel describes them:
  - Standard Protection protects previews and generated deployment URLs but not
    production domains.
  - All Deployments protects everything, including production.
  - (Legacy) Pre-Production Deployments protects only previews, so production
    stays public.

  Fastest path to a public production URL

  Try these in order, saving and testing after each:
  1. If "All Deployments" is selected, switch it to Standard Protection (or
     (Legacy) Pre-Production Deployments if it's listed), then click Save.
  2. Check Settings → Domains. Standard Protection treats only domains listed
     there as production domains. A bare generated address like
     chalo-project-f671.vercel.app may count as a generated URL and stay
     protected. If it's listed as a Production domain, step 1 is enough. If it
     isn't listed, step 3 is easier than adding it.
  3. Turn the Vercel Authentication toggle off and save. Everything becomes
     public, including previews. That's fine for a hello-world app, but remember
     it once real data is involved. You can switch it back on at M1, when the
     app has accounts.

  Hobby accounts can change this setting; paid plans aren't needed. The paid
  options are Password Protection and Trusted IPs, which we don't use.

  When you're done

  Tell me which option you ended up with. I'll re-check
  https://chalo-project-f671.vercel.app and run the full verification. If you
  can't find the toggle or the labels, send a screenshot or paste the page's
  text and I'll adapt.

● The values come from Supabase and go into Vercel. In total you add five
  entries.

  Where to get the values

  In Supabase, open a project, then Project Settings (gear icon), then API. You
  may see API Keys and Data API as separate pages. Copy:
  - Project URL, which looks like https://<ref>.supabase.co
  - the anon public key. If your dashboard only shows a publishable key
    (sb_publishable_…), use that. Both work with our client.

  Never use the service_role or secret key (ARC-004). These two values are meant
  to be public: the browser downloads them inside the app's JavaScript.

  Where to put them in Vercel

  1. Open the project's environment variables page:
     https://vercel.com/project-f671/chalo/settings/environment-variables. Or go
     to the chalo project, then Settings, then Environment Variables.
  2. Add each row below with Add (or Add Another). Leave the Sensitive toggle
     off, because Vite needs to read these at build time and they are public
     anyway.
  3. For Environments, uncheck All Environments and tick only the ones listed.
     You enter the same key twice, once for Production and once for Preview,
     with different values.

  ┌──────────────────────┬─────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┐
  │         Key          │ Environment │               Value                │
  │                      │      s      │                                    │
  ├──────────────────────┼─────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ VITE_SUPABASE_URL    │ Production  │ chalo-production Project URL       │
  │                      │ only        │                                    │
  ├──────────────────────┼─────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_K │ Production  │ chalo-production anon key          │
  │ EY                   │ only        │                                    │
  ├──────────────────────┼─────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ VITE_SUPABASE_URL    │ Preview     │ chalo-staging Project URL          │
  │                      │ only        │                                    │
  ├──────────────────────┼─────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_K │ Preview     │ chalo-staging anon key             │
  │ EY                   │ only        │                                    │
  ├──────────────────────┼─────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ VITE_APP_URL         │ Production  │ https://chalo-project-f671.vercel. │
  │                      │ only        │ app                                │
  └──────────────────────┴─────────────┴────────────────────────────────────┘

  Leave Development unticked everywhere. Local work uses .env, not Vercel. For a
  Preview variable, keep the branch field at its default, which applies it to
  all preview branches.

  Check yourself

  - Names must match exactly, with no spaces. If Vercel says a key already
    exists, you're probably adding it with All Environments selected; edit the
    first one's environments instead.
  - Which project goes where: Production uses chalo-production, and Preview uses
    chalo-staging. Mixing them up would point preview builds at your real
    production database.
  - Saving doesn't change existing deployments. The values are baked in at build
    time, so they apply from the next build.

● I found a real bug: PostgreSQL caps regex repetition at 255, so the spec's
  {2,256} UPI pattern is invalid there and would've failed in production. Since
  the migration has only run locally, I'll fix it now by splitting the rule into
  a regex plus a separate length check to preserve the exact spec behavior.

● Phase 1 of M1 is done: the database layer and its tests are committed and
  pushed to m1-accounts-groups as 98d1084. M1 as a whole is not done. CI is
  green on that commit, including a fresh database build, and the Vercel preview
  built.

  What exists now

  - Database tables: profiles, groups, members and invites, with the standard
    version columns, a sign-up trigger that creates each user's profile, and
    storage buckets for photos, bookings and receipts.
  - Access rules: row-level security everywhere, with narrow permissions so that
    anonymous visitors can't read any table. Triggers enforce the role rules,
    including "the last owner can't leave or be demoted".
  - Server functions:
    - create_group and create_invite (the token is generated in the database).
    - invite_preview, which is public.
    - accept_invite, which also lets someone take over a placeholder person.
    - health, for the keep-alive job.
  - Tests: 117 SQL assertions across 4 files, all passing.
  - Test strength: I also broke the security on purpose three ways (RLS off on
    members, the guard trigger dropped, viewers allowed to write). The tests
    failed each time, then a clean reset made them pass again.

  One thing the tests caught

  PostgreSQL won't accept the spec's UPI pattern ({2,256}), because its regex
  limit is 255. I kept the same rule by splitting it into a regex and a length
  check, and logged it in DECISIONS.md. Any client-side validation must use the
  original pattern.

  Not done yet

  - App code: nothing in the web app yet. That is Phases 2 to 4: sign-in
    screens, the groups UI and join page, and the sync engine.
  - Keep-alive workflow (DEP-005): not written yet.
  - Two-users E2E test: not written yet.
  - Production database: nothing has been pushed there yet. These migrations
    only exist locally and in CI.

  For you

  SETUP.md section E (Google sign-in) is still open. I don't need it for the
  next phase, because local development signs in with email links through a
  local test inbox. You need it before the DoD check that two real people join
  one group on staging.

  Tell me "continue" and I'll start Phase 2, the app foundations: Supabase
  client, sign-in screens and profile editing.

● Phase 2 is done and pushed as 992589e. All four CI jobs pass on that commit,
  including the new browser-test job that runs on a fresh stack.

  What you can do now

  - Sign in: with a Google button and an emailed link. There are no passwords.
  - Come back where you were: after signing in, you return to the page you were
    heading for.
  - Edit your profile: name, UPI ID and Instagram handle, with the validation
    rules from the spec, and sign out.

  How I tested it

  - Unit tests: 19, covering the env checks, the profile rules and the redirect
    guard that stops ?next= sending people to another site.
  - Real browser runs: against the local stack, an actual emailed link was read
    from a local mail catcher. The flow was: sign in, auto-created profile,
    validation errors, saved edits that survive a reload, sign out, and back to
    the page you wanted. This also proves the earlier database permissions work
    from the real client.
  - CI: now runs these on every push as the e2e-backend job.

  Not tested

  - Google sign-in: only the button exists. It won't work until you finish
    SETUP.md E, so a failed Google attempt on staging or production is expected
    until then.
  - Email links on the hosted projects: Supabase's built-in email sender is
    heavily rate-limited, as SETUP.md warns.

  Note for later

  The JS bundle is 176 KB gzipped against the 250 KB budget. There's headroom,
  but lazy-loading is already needed for the heavy modules, as the spec
  requires.

  Next

  Phase 3 is the groups UI: create a group, the members list, placeholder
  people, invite links, the /join/:token page and roles. Tell me when SETUP.md E
  is done, or just say "continue" and I'll start Phase 3.

● In SETUP.md step E.7, the two Supabase projects get different values. For
  staging, you don't add a "production URL" at all. I've updated SETUP.md with
  this table and pushed it (548f1bf).

  Supabase → Authentication → URL Configuration

  Setting: Site URL
  chalo-staging: http://localhost:5173
  chalo-production: https://chalo-project-f671.vercel.app
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Setting: Redirect URLs (one entry each, using Add URL)
  chalo-staging: http://localhost:5173/**
  chalo-production: https://chalo-project-f671.vercel.app
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Setting:
  chalo-staging: https://*-project-f671.vercel.app
  chalo-production: https://chalo-project-f671.vercel.app/**
  ────────────────────────────────────────
  Setting:
  chalo-staging: https://*-project-f671.vercel.app/**
  chalo-production:

  Click Save changes in each project.

  Why they differ

  - Staging serves previews and local development. Vercel preview builds use the
    staging Supabase project, and local development runs on localhost:5173.
    Previews have changing addresses such as
    chalo-git-<branch>-project-f671.vercel.app, so the *-project-f671.vercel.app
    wildcard covers all of them.
  - Production allows only its own address. A preview build can then never sign
    someone in against the real database.
  - The Site URL is only a fallback. The app always asks to return to the
    address it's running on. The Site URL is used only if that redirect is
    rejected, so a bad value won't break normal sign-in.

  Two things to check

  - The wildcard form is from memory of Supabase's docs. I haven't tested it
    against your projects. After saving, sign in once from a Vercel preview URL
    of the m1-accounts-groups branch. If you're sent to localhost:5173 instead,
    tell me; the wildcard hasn't matched, and I'll switch to listing the exact
    preview address.
  - The Google client has its own list. In Google Cloud, the OAuth client's
    redirect URIs must be the two Supabase callback URLs from E.4
    (https://<ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback). Those are not the Vercel
    addresses.

  When E is done, tell me and I'll continue with Phase 3, the groups UI.

● Phase 3 is done and pushed as f7cb48a. All CI jobs pass, including the browser
  test with five users. The production database is still empty, and I haven't
  pushed these migrations anywhere hosted.

  What works now

  - Trips: a home list of your trips, and a Create a trip form with name,
    optional dates, time zone and currency.
  - People: the group page shows everyone with their role. Owners and admins can
    change roles, and the database refuses to leave a trip without an owner.
  - Placeholders: add a friend by name before they have an account.
  - Invite links: ordinary links, plus links that hand someone a specific
    placeholder's name. Claim links are single-use. Admins can copy, share and
    revoke links.
  - Join page: /join/:token is public, so anyone can see what they're joining
    before signing in. Joining requires an account.

  How it was tested

  - Unit tests: 45 in total, covering role rules, form validation, error
    mapping, and date and time formatting.
  - E2E-1: passes three runs in a row against the local stack with five separate
    browser sessions. It covers:
    - creating a trip and the validation errors on the form;
    - the owner adding a placeholder and creating both kinds of invite;
    - Bala joining from a signed-out link, and seeing no owner tools;
    - Chitra claiming Zed's name, with the person count staying at 3, and the
      claim link then being used up;
    - Alice making Bala a viewer, and the last owner being unable to step down;
    - a non-member seeing nothing.
  - A test bug I fixed: my first run raced the sign-in, so a person arrived
    signed out. The helper now waits for the session to be stored.

  Known gaps

  - Live updates: another person's change shows after a reload. Phase 4 adds
    live sync.
  - Leaving a trip: there's no leave button yet (GRP-006). It needs balances,
    which arrive in M2. The database rule is already tested.
  - Bundle size: the main JS is 182.5 KB gzipped, against the 250 KB budget.

  Needs your decision

  The hosted staging database has no tables yet, so Vercel previews can't use
  the groups features there. I can run the migrations on staging through the
  deploy-db.yml workflow, which is what it's for. It's your call, because it
  changes a hosted database. It does not touch production. Say "push the
  database to staging" if you want it; Google sign-in on previews also still
  depends on your SETUP.md section E.

  Next

  Phase 4 is the sync backbone: the offline Dexie database, the outbox for
  queued writes, the table registry, pulling changes, live updates, and the sync
  status indicator (SYN-001 to SYN-005, SYN-008). It's the largest part of M1.
  Say "continue" to start it.

● Phases 4 and 5 are mostly done, but M1 is not finished. What's left needs your

  (90938a0) is pushed but I haven't checked its CI.

  What's built

  - Local-first data: trips and people are stored on the device (Dexie) first,
    with a queue of unsent changes.
  - Sync: changes go to the server in order. Pulls fetch only what changed, with
    a one-minute overlap so late commits aren't missed. Live updates arrive
    through Realtime, with focus, reconnect and a 60-second timer as fallbacks.
  - Conflicts: last write wins, and an unsent local change is never overwritten
    by a pull.
  - Refused changes: if the server refuses a change, it isn't silently dropped.
    The device goes back to the server's value, and the refused change stays in
    a status panel with Retry and Dismiss.
  - Status indicator: shows offline, syncing, waiting, or "could not be saved".
  - Keep-alive workflow (DEP-005): keepalive.yml calls the health() function
    weekly on both Supabase projects. I checked the request against the local
    stack, but it hasn't run on GitHub yet.

  How it was tested

  - Unit tests: 71, including 22 for the sync engine against an in-memory fake
    server.
  - Browser tests: 11, each run five times in parallel with no failures. They
    cover live updates between two people, a whole offline session that reaches
    the server on reconnect (checked from a fresh device), and two people
    editing the same row.
  - What the tests found:
    - TanStack Query froze offline writes, because it pauses mutations offline
      by default. That's fixed.
    - Two timing and selector bugs were in my own tests, not the product. Those
      are fixed too.

  Needs your attention

  - Bundle size: the initial JavaScript is 219 KB gzipped against the 250 KB
    budget. Route-level lazy loading needs to come before the next big feature.
  - Hosted databases: neither Supabase project has the migrations yet. Previews,
    the keep-alive and the DoD check on staging all need them.

  5. Then I'll open the M1 pull request. I'll push the database to production
     and tag m1 only after you approve each step.

● M3 is built and open as PR #7:
  https://github.com/mahawarrajul-bot/Chalo/pull/7. All CI checks pass (unit and
  coverage, SQL tests, browser tests, and the Vercel preview). I haven't merged
  anything.

  What's in it
  - Itemised bills: a bill editor where you tap the people who shared each item,
    with an "Everyone" shortcut. You can give someone extra shares by button or
    by press-and-hold. It handles taxes, service charges, tips, discounts and
    round-offs. Saving is blocked until the lines add up to the printed total.
    If they're off by under ₹5, one tap adds the round-off.
  - Explain my share: it shows the working for any person on the bill, using the
    same engine that saved the shares. It warns if the saved share differs from
    the working.
  - Foreign currencies: the expense form has a currency and exchange rate, with
    a preview of the trip-currency amount. "Look up the rate" asks the free
    Frankfurter service, only when tapped. If it fails, you type the rate, and
    saving never depends on it.
  - Filters: search by text, person, category and date range on the Money
    screen. They work offline.
  - Database and sync: items, who had each item, and charges now sync with the
    expense. The server checks that items plus charges equal the total, and a
    new ITEMS_MISMATCH error covers a mismatch.

  Definition of done: the browser tests enter TV-3 and TV-4 through the UI. They
  compare every share, balance, suggested payment and "Explain my share" line
  with Appendix A. The new bill tests passed 30 of 30 when repeated five times
  in parallel.

  Test totals: 328 unit tests, core coverage 100%, 225 SQL assertions, and 23
  browser tests.

  One thing I fixed along the way: charges were coming back in random order
  after every save, so I added a position column. That meant editing the new
  migration, which has only run on my local database. I reset that database.
  Nothing on staging or production changed.

  Needs your decision
  1. Merge: PRs #6 (M2 close-out) and #7 are both open. Both edit SPEC.md, so
     merge #6 first or expect a small conflict.
  2. Push to the databases: the new migration is local only. I can push it to
     staging and then production through deploy-db.yml when you approve.
  3. Spec change: I proposed three changes in docs/SPEC_CHANGES.md. They add the
     position column, name ITEMS_MISMATCH, and allow api.frankfurter.dev in the
     content security policy (connect-src in vercel.json) for the optional rate
     lookup. I haven't edited SPEC.md for these, since that waits on your
     approval.

  Known issues
  - The first download is about 232 KB gzipped against the 250 KB limit, so
    there is little headroom left.
  - Frankfurter doesn't publish every currency (AED, for example), so some rates
    must be typed.
  - A bill whose round-off or discount would leave someone with a negative share
    is refused with a generic message.

  M3 is closed out first. PR #6 and PR #7 are merged, the itemised-bills
  migration is on staging and production, and the SPEC change from M3 is
  approved and applied.

  What M4 delivers
  - Plan: every day of the trip, with add, edit and delete, status (proposed
    plans look different), times, place, notes and estimated cost.
  - Reorder: by dragging (pointer, touch and keyboard) or by move up/down
    buttons.
  - Place search and map:
    - Place search uses Nominatim, runs only when you press Search, is limited
      to one request every 1.1 seconds, and answers are kept on the device.
    - You can also tap the map to set a pin.
    - The map has Leaflet with numbered markers, a line per day, and the "©
      OpenStreetMap contributors" attribution.
  - Travel estimates: an approximate travel time between consecutive plans with
    a place, plus a warning when you'd arrive after the next plan starts.
  - Polls: 2 to 6 options with live results and one changeable vote each. An
    owner or admin closes it, and a proposal poll's winner becomes a confirmed
    plan. A tie is the closer's choice.
  - Today card: shown on the trip home during the trip.
  - Expense links: an expense can belong to a plan, and the plan lists it.

  Definition of done
  - Two browsers edit one itinerary at once and both edits survive. For the same
    plan, the last write wins.
  - A poll closes into a confirmed plan on both devices.
  - The map shows numbered markers.

  Test results: 415 unit tests, core coverage at 100%, 310 SQL assertions, and
  29 browser tests. The six new browser tests passed 24 of 24 when repeated four
  times in parallel.

  One thing I added for safety: the browser tests now run under the production
  content security policy from vercel.json. All 23 earlier tests still pass
  under it.

  Needs your decision
  1. Merge PR #8.
  2. Push the migration 20261016000200_itinerary.sql to staging and then
     production. It is local only so far.
  3. SPEC change proposal in docs/SPEC_CHANGES.md. It covers
     poll_options.position, moving the bookings foreign key to M5, naming
     POLL_CLOSED and OPTION_NOT_LEADING, and two new hosts in the content
     security policy (tile.openstreetmap.org and nominatim.openstreetmap.org). I
     haven't edited SPEC.md for these.
  4. New dependencies: Leaflet (BSD-2-Clause) and dnd-kit (MIT). Neither is a
     tracker or paid.

  Gaps and known issues
  - Booking links (ITN-010): linking a plan to a booking waits for M5, since
    bookings don't exist yet.
  - Today card shortcuts: the "next booking" and "add photo" shortcuts also wait
    (M5 and M6).
  - Dragging to another day: not supported. You change the plan's day in the
    form instead.
  - Bundle size: the first download is about 236 KB gzipped against the 250 KB
    limit, so about 14 KB of headroom is left. The map and drag-and-drop load
    only on the screens that use them.
  - Poll closing time: it's read in the person's own time zone, not the trip's.
  - PR description: I first created the PR with a stale description left over
    from earlier. I corrected it right away.

  The next milestone is M5 (bookings and tickets vault). Tell me which of the
  decisions above to act on, and whether to start M5 now.

● I approved and did all of M4's items. M5 (bookings and tickets vault) is built
  and open as PR #9: https://github.com/mahawarrajul-bot/Chalo/pull/9. All CI
  checks pass (unit and coverage, SQL tests, browser tests, Vercel preview). I
  have not merged it or touched staging or production for M5.

  M4 close-out

  - PR #8 is merged.
  - SPEC change is applied to SPEC.md (itinerary, polls and the content security
    policy hosts).
  - Migration 20261016000200 is on staging and production, and keep-alive is
    green for both.
  - Tags m3 and m4 are pushed. You hadn't listed tagging, but it's part of the
    milestone workflow.

  CI failed twice before it passed. A floating-point property test failed on one
  random seed, and the same-plan conflict test raced because Alice could
  reconnect before Bala's write reached the server. Both were test problems, not
  app bugs, and both are fixed.

  What M5 delivers

  - Bookings: add, edit and delete, with times typed where they happen (the
    trip's time zone, daylight saving handled), amount, travellers and seats.
    They work offline.
  - Ticket files: PDF, JPG, PNG or WebP, up to 5 MB each and 5 per booking.
    Rules are checked on both the phone and the server.
  - Viewer: full screen for images and PDFs, with zoom by pinch, buttons,
    double-tap and Ctrl+wheel. It keeps the screen on while a ticket is open.
  - My tickets: every booking that lists you as a traveller, across all trips,
    grouped by date.
  - Coming up: a countdown, plus a banner within a day of the next departure.
  - Links: an expense can be started from a booking, and plans can link to a
    booking.

  Definition of done: the browser test attaches a real PDF and a real PNG, opens
  each once online, turns the connection off, and opens both again.

  Test results: 470 unit tests, core coverage at 100%, 376 SQL assertions, and
  35 browser tests. The six new browser tests passed 18 of 18 under parallel
  load.

  Needs your decision

  1. Merge PR #9.
  2. Push the migration 20261016000300_bookings.sql to staging and then
     production. It's local only so far.
  3. Spec change proposal in docs/SPEC_CHANGES.md: a stable error code
     TOO_MANY_FILES, PDFs shown with pdfjs-dist, and checks on bookings. I
     haven't edited SPEC.md for it.
  4. New dependency: pdfjs-dist (Apache-2.0, no tracker). It loads only when a
     PDF is opened.

  Gaps and known issues

  - Attaching files needs a connection. The booking itself works offline and
    says why attaching waits.
  - Storage guard (the 90% cap) is M6's. Until then only the 5 MB and 5-file
    limits protect storage.
  - Pinch zoom isn't tested with a real two-finger gesture, because Playwright
    can't do one. The button zoom is tested.
  - Bundle size: the first download is about 242 KB gzipped against the 250 KB
    limit, so about 8 KB of headroom. M6 should trim or split before adding to
    the first screen.

  The next milestone is M6 (photos). Tell me which of the decisions above to act
  on, and whether to start M6 now.

● Before M6 I did the three things you approved for M5. I merged PR #9, pushed
  the bookings migration (staging, then production), and applied the approved
  spec change. pdfjs-dist is accepted too. I also tagged m5. Keep-alive is green
  for both databases.

  M6 (photos) is built and open as PR #10:
  https://github.com/mahawarrajul-bot/Chalo/pull/10. All CI checks pass. I have
  not merged it or touched staging or production for M6.

  What M6 delivers

  - Adding photos: from the gallery (several at once) or the camera. Each
    picture is processed on the phone: the date and place are read from it, it
    is made upright and no larger than 1600 px, a 480 px thumbnail is made, and
    the uploaded files carry no EXIF.
  - Upload queue: 3 at a time with retries. It survives closing the app and
    waits while offline. A photo the server refuses stops with its reason and a
    Retry button.
  - Dates: a photo with no date is marked "Date guessed", and the date can be
    corrected.
  - Album: filters by day, place and uploader that combine, infinite scroll, and
    a full-screen viewer with swipe, arrow keys and zoom.
  - Places: a photo near a plan that has a place (within 1.5 km) is named after
    it. Otherwise it is grouped as "Unnamed place", and naming one names every
    photo in that small area.
  - Location sharing: an option not to keep where photos were taken.
  - Duplicates: a photo that looks like one already in the album is held until
    you choose "Upload anyway" or "Skip it".
  - Delete: the uploader, an owner or an admin can delete a photo, and its files
    are removed at once.
  - Storage guard: new photos are blocked at 90% of the 900 MB cap. The server
    also refuses at its own hard limit of 1000 MB.

  Definition of done: 20 real JPEGs with EXIF upload from the page. The day,
  place and uploader filters match the numbers expected from the trip's dates
  and the plan's place. The storage guard is tested in the browser and at the
  server's hard limit.

  Test results: 556 unit tests, core coverage at 100%, 445 SQL assertions, and
  41 browser tests. The six new browser tests passed 24 of 24 under parallel
  load.

  Needs your decision

  1. Merge PR #10.
  2. Push the migration 20261016000400_photos.sql to staging and then
     production. It is local only so far.
  3. Spec change proposal in docs/SPEC_CHANGES.md. It covers a new value
     taken_at_source = 'manual', the share-location check, the stable code
     STORAGE_FULL, and that photo rows are written only through four functions.
     I haven't edited SPEC.md for it.
  4. There is no new dependency this time.

  Gaps and known issues

  - Bundle size is the real risk. The first download is about 245 KB gzipped
    against the 250 KB limit, so only about 5 KB of headroom is left. The next
    milestone should trim first. The text of the whole app is one eager module
    and is the obvious thing to split.
  - Not done: the "By person" filter (it needs face tags, M7), reverse geocoding
    (P2), the sharpness score (P2) and ZIP download (P2).
  - Offline edits: editing and deleting a photo need a connection.
  - Orphan files: if the app is closed between recording a deletion and removing
    the files, an orphan file can stay in storage. There is no clean-up sweep
    yet.
  - Slow tests: two earlier edit-conflict tests were running close to their 30 s
    limit under load. I gave them more time.

  The next milestone is M7 (face matching). That one involves personal data, so
  under the working agreement I'll stop and ask you before changing how face
  data is handled. Tell me which of the decisions above to act on, and whether
  to start M7 planning now.

● M7 is built and PR #11 is open with every check green: lint, typecheck, unit
  tests, 544 database assertions, and the full browser suite. I've stopped
  before merging, deploying or tagging because those need your approval.

  What works
  - DoD met, with a stand-in face model: three members who opted in are
    auto-tagged on a test set, a member who didn't is never tagged, and
    withdrawal removes the fingerprint, the consent and the tags.
  - Withdrawal covers the manual tags too: deleting your face data removes the
    tags the app made, and optionally the ones people added by hand.
  - Real model: it loads from the app's own address, runs in the browser, and
    makes no request to anyone else.
  - Tests: 611 unit, 544 database assertions (99 new, mutation-checked) and 45
    browser tests (4 new, 16 of 16 under parallel load).
  - Two fixes along the way:
    - A race where a photo was scanned before its row reached the phone.
    - A flaky M6 upload-queue test.
  - One rare flake: one run of the whole browser suite failed the M5 offline-PDF
    test. It passed 24 of 24 on repeat.

  What is not verified
  - Accuracy on real faces: this hasn't been tested, and I can't here. The
    starting threshold of 0.90 is an unmeasured placeholder, so someone must run
    docs/FACE_TUNING.md with the team's own photos (low light, varied skin
    tones) before relying on it.
  - First download: about 248 KB gzipped against the 250 KB limit, so under 2 KB
    of headroom. The next feature that adds code to the first screen must first
    move something out. The app's text in messages.ts is the obvious candidate.

  Decisions for you
  1. Face-data clarifications. These go beyond the spec text and are in
     docs/SPEC_CHANGES.md. All of them reduce face data:
     - Consent is per trip.
     - Leaving or being removed deletes your fingerprint.
     - Consent can only change through the enrol and withdraw actions.
     - A photo is rescanned only for people who opted in after it was last
       scanned.
       Do you approve them?
  2. Merge PR #11?
  3. Push migration 20261016000500_faces.sql to staging, then production (deploy
     from main)?
  4. Tag m7 after the merge?

● M8 is built and PR #12 is open. All CI checks are green (lint, typecheck, 671
  unit tests, 544 database assertions, 48 browser tests) and the Vercel preview
  built.

  What works
  - Scan a bill: "Scan a bill" in the expense form reads a photo with a reader
    that runs on the phone. It fills the existing itemised form with items, CGST
    + SGST as one tax line, service charge, discount, round-off, the total and
    the date.
  - Review before saving: the scan never saves anything. Nobody is assigned to
    any item, uncertain lines are highlighted, and saving is refused until the
    person ticks "I have checked every line".
  - Real reader tested: the browser tests read a drawn bill with the real reader
    inside the production security policy. The edge cases below came out of
    that.
  - Photo of the bill:
    - The compressed photo is kept by default, in the private receipts bucket.
    - A bill scanned and saved offline uploads its photo when the connection
      returns.
    - Scanning works offline once the reader has been downloaded once.
  - PDF prefill (BKG-007): "Fill in from a PDF" in the booking form fills only
    empty boxes and says which.

  Things worth knowing
  - Security policy change: the script-src directive gains 'wasm-unsafe-eval',
    because the reader is WebAssembly. It doesn't allow eval of text, and I
    changed nothing else. It's recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md.
  - Reader files: the reader's files are served from the app itself, not from a
    CDN.
  - First download: about 246 KB gzipped against the 250 KB limit. It had crept
    up to about 253 KB (over the limit) once the new parsers were added; marking
    @chalo/core as side-effect free brought it below where it was before M8.
  - CI fix: CI first failed because pnpm treats the unreviewed install script in
    tesseract.js (a donation banner) as an error. I declared it not allowed in
    pnpm-workspace.yaml.
  - Flaky test: the M5 offline-ticket test twice ran out of its 30 s default in
    a full single-worker run on this machine. It passes alone and in parallel,
    and now uses test.slow().

  Not verified
  I haven't tested accuracy on real crumpled or thermal receipts or phone-camera
  photos. The reader is good on clean printed text, and correcting the draft is
  the supported path. A manual check with a few real bills is worth doing.

  Decisions for you
  1. Merge PR #12?
  2. Tag m8 after the merge?
  3. There is no database migration this time, so nothing needs deploying.
     Merging ships the app through Vercel.

  After that, M9 (Instagram studio) is next.

● M9 is built and PR #13 is open. All CI checks are green (lint, typecheck, 751
  unit tests, 544 database assertions, 53 browser tests) and the Vercel preview
  deployed. I've stopped before merging and tagging, and there is one decision I
  need from you.

  What works
  - Templates: all six render at the right sizes (1080×1920 for stories,
    1080×1350 for the feed collage). The browser tests decode the downloaded
    JPEGs and check the colour at the middle of every slot against the photo
    that belongs there.
  - Auto-pick and sharpness: auto-pick prefers sharp photos and tagged ones,
    with at most one photo per 10 minutes. Sharpness is measured on the phone
    from thumbnails and cached, so it needs no database change and works for
    older photos.
  - Privacy:
    - The studio has day and place filters only, with no person filter.
    - "My trip" uses only photos you are tagged in.
    - Only members who added an Instagram name can be tagged, and each can be
      switched off.
    - The review step lists who appears and shows the "only post what everyone
      would be comfortable with" reminder.
  - Reel: a reel records as a real 1080×1920 video, with progress and a cancel
    button, and no sound.
  - Share: the share sheet opens with the picture and caption where the browser
    can. Otherwise the picture downloads, the caption is copied and the person
    is told what to do next.
  - CSP fix: the reel wouldn't play because the Content-Security-Policy had no
    media-src. I added media-src 'self' blob:, which is the only change to the
    policy.
  - First download: unchanged at about 246 KB gzipped; the studio loads on
    demand.

  Needs your decision: FFmpeg
  The spec says a browser that can only record WebM should be offered a
  conversion to MP4 using FFmpeg compiled to WebAssembly. The only npm build of
  it, @ffmpeg/core, is GPL-2.0-or-later and 65 MB, so I haven't added it. For
  now a WebM-only browser gets the WebM with a note that Instagram may not
  accept it. Chrome on Android records MP4 directly, so the main path isn't
  affected. You can approve the GPL package (loaded on demand, never in the
  first download) or accept WebM-only for v1.

  Not verified
  - Share on a real phone: I haven't tried the share sheet on a real Android
    phone, because the tests stub navigator.share, and I don't know whether
    Instagram accepts the files.
  - Reel format: headless Chromium records WebM, so I haven't seen which format
    real phones produce.
  - Android share path: the Capacitor share path for the Android build belongs
    to M10.

  Questions for you
  1. Merge PR #13?
  2. Tag m9 after the merge?
  3. FFmpeg: approve the GPL package, or accept WebM-only for v1?

  There is no database migration, so nothing needs deploying beyond the merge.
  After that, M10 (Android, privacy and hardening) is next.

      32  - **Context:** UX-004 asks for one warm, travel-inspired identi
          ty (palette, one typeface, rounded cards), recorded here. The a
          pp has used one since M1 but it was never written down.
      33  - **Decision:**
      34 -  - **Palette:** "sunset and chai". Page background a warm crea
         -m (Tailwind `orange-50`, `#fdf3e3` on the install splash), text
         - warm black (`stone-900`), primary actions terracotta (`orange-
         -700` with white text, `#c25b3a` as the browser and install them
         -e colour), cards and dividers a pale apricot (`orange-200`), ne
         -utrals from the `stone` scale. Dark mode (UX-001) follows the p
         -hone: near-black warm background (`stone-950`), cream text, the
         - primary action one step lighter (`orange-600`) so contrast hol
         -ds. Colour is never the only signal (statuses also carry words)
         -, and body text and controls were checked at 4.5:1 or better (t
         -he Lighthouse accessibility audit scores 100).                 
      34 +  - **Palette:** "sunset and chai". Page background a warm crea
         +m (Tailwind `orange-50`, `#fdf3e3` on the install splash), text

         +utrals from the `stone` scale. Dark mode (UX-001) follows the p
         +hone: near-black warm background (`stone-950`), cream text, the
         + primary action one step lighter (`orange-600`) so contrast hol
         +ds. Colour is never the only signal (statuses also carry words)

         +me colours but have not been audited one by one.

          pp is read in is supported.

          ns.mjs`); replace them, and Capacitor's default launcher icon,

  │ 400  │ The request was malformed or the sign-in token was rejected.      │
  ├──────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 415  │ The server didn't accept the file type. The photo bucket takes    │
  │      │ only JPEG.                                                        │
  ├──────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 422  │ The server couldn't process the request, for example an odd file  │
  │      │ or name.                                                          │
  ├──────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 409  │ The file already exists. The app normally treats that as fine.    │
  └──────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Anything over 500 is retried by the app, so you wouldn't see it as "refused".
  Two limits are in the server settings: JPEG only, and 5 MB per file. Too large
  is shown as its own message, so size is unlikely here.

● I found the real cause of the reminders switch, and the fix is on PR #20. It's
  not merged yet, and CI is still finishing: the push run passed and the
  pull-request run is in progress.

  The cause was a bug in the app, not your phone. Capacitor's notification
  plugin answers to any property name, including then. My code handed the plugin
  back from an async function, so JavaScript treated it as a promise. It sent a
  call named "then" to the phone, and nothing ever answered. So the permission
  step waited forever, even though notifications were allowed for Chalo. The
  share sheet and sign-in link weren't affected because they load their plugins
  differently.

  What I did:
  - The app now hands on a plain object of its own that calls the plugin's
    methods.
  - A new test reproduces the hang with a stand-in that behaves like Capacitor's
    plugin. With the old code both tests time out, and with the fix they pass.
  - All 888 unit tests pass.

● M11 is built and on PR #22, with CI green on the latest commit. It isn't
  merged, and nothing has been applied to staging or production. One item,
  BKG-008, is not built and needs your decision.

  What was built, with tests
  - Archive a trip (GRP-008): the owner archives it after a second tap. Everyone
    can still read it, nobody can add or change anything, and the owner can
    open it again. One database rule refuses every content write, including
    files. A browser test sends a rename straight to the database and sees it
    refused.
  - Comments on an expense (EXP-009): written once and never edited. The author
    or an admin can remove one, and nobody can write as someone else.
  - Packing list (ITN-012): shared, with who brings what and a count, linked
    from the trip page.
  - Printing the plan and the packing list (ITN-011): they print as plain words,
    without menus or buttons.
  - Saved expenses (EXP-010): save an expense and add it again in a tap, or add
    it for every day of the trip (up to 60 days, only when you ask).
  - Saved bill layouts (TAX-009): a bill's taxes, service charge, tip and
    discount are saved as percentages and fill the next bill. The printed-total
    check still decides whether it can be saved.
  - ZIP of photos (PHO-011): downloads the photos the album is showing as one
    file, up to 200 photos or 100 MB.
  - Backup (DEP-010): scripts/export-db.sh and docs/BACKUP.md. I tried a restore
    on the local database and the counts matched exactly (565 trips, 955
    people, 285 expenses, 809 accounts).
  - Also: EXP-022 was already built, so I just named it in the tests. "Download
    my data" and the privacy page now cover the comments and packing items.

  Checks: 958 unit tests, 703 database assertions (59 new; eight deliberate
  breaks were each caught), and 76 browser tests. First download is 184 KB. All
  84 P0 requirements are covered.

  CI caught one real bug in my own work: the packing and comment forms cleared
  only after saving, so on a slow machine a quick second entry was wiped. I
  fixed that and CI is green. The browser suite still shows the same occasional
  slow-run timeouts as before. They pass when run alone.

  What I need from you
  1. Decide on BKG-008 (secure documents). It would store ID and passport
     numbers, encrypted on the phone with a passphrase that never leaves it, in
     a new server table. That's a new kind of sensitive data, so I didn't build
     it. Say yes and I build it with the privacy page and account deletion
     extended. Say no and it stays out.
  2. Approve the spec change in docs/SPEC_CHANGES.md: groups.archived_at and the
     new comments and templates tables.
  3. Say "merge" when you're ready. Then run Deploy DB for staging and
     production to apply the new migration. Until it's applied, a project can't
     write comments, packing items or templates, or archive a trip. Take a
     backup first with docs/BACKUP.md.

  Known limits:
  - Archiving doesn't block role changes or invites, though the screens don't
    offer them.
  - I haven't checked the ZIP on a real phone, or printed to paper.

● I've written the shared playlist proposal into docs/SPEC_CHANGES.md and opened
  it as docs-only PR #25. Nothing is built yet and no migration is written.

  What you'd get
  - A shared playlist per trip. Anyone who can write adds a song (title,
    optional artist and note), and it shows who added it. Viewers can read but
    not add.
  - One vote each. People can take a vote back. The list is ordered by votes,
    then oldest first, so every phone shows the same order.
  - Played and removed. Anyone can mark a song played, which moves it to a
    "Played" section, and put it back. The person who added a song, or an admin,
    can remove it.
  - No doubles. Adding a song that's already there offers a vote for it instead.
  - Search links, no playing. Each song gets buttons that open a search for it
    in Spotify or YouTube Music. There's also a button that copies the list as
    text, to paste into a playlist app.
  - Live and offline. It works with no connection and updates on everyone's
    phone like the rest of the app.
  - The usual rules. An archived trip's list is read-only. A deleted account's
    songs stay as "Former member" and their votes are removed. "Download my
    data" and the privacy page cover it.

  What it deliberately isn't: a music player or a link to a streaming account.
  There's no audio, no sign-in, no API keys and no embedded players, because
  those would load code from other companies and break the no-trackers rule.

  What it needs: two new database tables and a small screen. No new paid
  service, dependency or kind of personal data. Song choices say a little about
  someone's taste, so the privacy page will say who can see them: people on the
  same trip.

  Your next step: read the entry in docs/SPEC_CHANGES.md and tell me "approve",
  or what to change (for example no voting after all, or a different limit on
  lengths). I'll then build it in the usual order, with tests first, then the
  database, the screen, and browser tests. I'll ask before merging and before
  deploying the migration.

  PR #24 (the M11 closeout notes) is still open too. Say "merge" for either or
  both.

● Here is everything Chalo does, grouped as in SPEC.md. Every group is built and
  has tests except two optional P3 items (BKG-009, IGS-011), which are
  deliberately not built.

  Accounts and trips
  - Sign in with Google or an emailed link. There are no passwords and no SMS
    codes.
  - Profile with name, avatar, UPI ID and Instagram handle.
  - Create a trip with name, dates, time zone and currency.
  - Invite links with a role and an expiry. Someone joining can take over a
    placeholder person.
  - Add people who have no account yet.
  - Roles: owner, admin, member and viewer.
  - Leaving a trip, and an archived trip that is read-only for everyone.
  - Trip home with a countdown, spend against budget, your balance, the next
    booking and a "Today" view.
  - Activity feed that links to what changed.

  Money
  - Expenses with title, amount, currency, date and category. They can be edited
    and deleted.
  - Splits: equal, exact amounts, percent and shares. Several people can pay one
    expense.
  - Itemised bills with fair tax sharing: per-item tax classes, service charge,
    tip, discount and round-off. Items can be shared unevenly with
    press-and-hold.
  - Multi-currency with a rate you type or look up.
  - Search and filter, trip budget with per-category totals, comments on an
    expense, and saved templates, including "add for every day of the trip".
  - Balances that always sum to zero, simplified suggestions for who pays whom,
    and settling up.
  - "Pay with UPI" link, WhatsApp or share-sheet reminders, and CSV export.
  - Receipt scanning on the phone, which reads the bill and fills in the items.
  - An expense can be created from a booking or a plan item.

  Plan
  - Day-by-day plan with drag-and-drop and move buttons, a map with numbered
    markers, place search and travel-time estimates.
  - Status flow of proposed, confirmed and cancelled.
  - Polls, which can turn the winning option into a plan item. Items link to
    bookings and expenses.
  - Printable plan and a shared packing list.

  Bookings and tickets
  - Bookings for flights, trains, hotels and more, with files attached.
  - Tickets open offline, a "My tickets" page, and an upcoming timeline.
  - Reminders on the Android app.
  - PDF prefill, and secure documents for ID or passport numbers, locked on the
    phone with a passphrase.

  Photos and faces
  - Upload from the gallery or camera through an offline-safe queue. EXIF data
    is read on the phone and the place is not kept unless you let it.
  - Album views by day, place, person and uploader, with duplicate warnings and
    a ZIP download.
  - Optional "Find me in photos": your phone makes a face fingerprint, matching
    runs on devices, and anyone can tag by hand. "Check this" tags need one tap
    to confirm. You can delete your face data at any time.

  Instagram studio
  - Story, post and carousel templates, and a Reel slideshow.
  - Auto-picking of the sharpest photos, captions and handle tags, a review
    step, and sharing through the phone's share sheet. Nothing is published
    automatically.
  - "My recap" and "Group recap".

  Trip playlist (the newest)
  - Everyone adds songs, with one vote each and the same order on every phone.
  - Songs can be marked as played, and duplicates are caught. Each song has
    search links into Spotify or YouTube Music, and the list can be copied as
    text. Chalo plays no audio.

  Works offline, and privacy
  - Everything is kept on the phone and syncs when the connection returns.
  - It installs as an app and has an Android build.
  - A sync status indicator shows pending and failed changes.
  - A plain-language privacy page, download of your data, deletion of your
    account or a trip, and no trackers or ads.

  Not built, on purpose
  - Email-forwarding of bookings (BKG-009).
  - Direct publishing to Instagram (IGS-011).

  If you'd like a deeper description of any group, or want me to compare this
  list against a feature you have in mind, tell me which.
